title: On the road
subtitle: traffic lights, get lost, brake, crash
summary: Talk about roads and road signs, describe how you found your way, and tell the story of an accident.

lesson.heading: Parts of a road
rows: the red, amber and green lights that stop and start the traffic
the place where two roads meet
a curve in the road; *this road bends to the right*
the place where people can cross the road
it carries the road over a river or another road
a big fast road between cities
part of a road separated from other parts by a line
the place at the side of the road where people walk

lesson.heading: Road signs
lesson.text: A **road sign** is a message or symbol beside the road that gives information. Common ones are the **speed limit** (for example 50 mph) and **no overtaking**, which means you can't pass another car.

examples.text: He was driving over the **speed limit**.
There's a **no overtaking** sign before the bend.
On a motorway, the **inside** or **slow lane** is for slower cars and the **outside** or **fast lane** is for faster ones.

lesson.heading: Finding your way
lesson.text: If you **get lost**, you don't know where you are. You can **ask someone the way** and they will **direct** you - tell you how to get to a place.

examples.text: Yesterday I **got lost** on my way to the airport.
I decided to go **via** the village of Pensford.
examples.note: via = through a place to get to a destination

examples.text: I took the wrong **turning** just before I got there.
examples.note: a turning = a corner where one road meets another

examples.text: I **ended up** in a supermarket car park.
examples.note: end up = find yourself in a place you didn't expect

examples.text: A kind woman **directed** me to the A38.

lesson.heading: Phrases for journeys
rows: go through one place to get to another
find yourself somewhere you didn't expect
ask how to get to a place
tell them how to get to a place

lesson.heading: An accident
lesson.text: A **pedestrian** is a person walking. If a car is **approaching**, it is coming closer. The driver **brakes** to stop, but the car may **swerve** - change direction suddenly and without control - and **crash into** something.

examples.text: I saw an **accident** this morning on the **main road** into town.
A **pedestrian** stepped off the **pavement** just as a car was **approaching**.
The driver **braked**, but the car **swerved** and **crashed into** a **parked car**.
The driver wasn't **injured**, but both cars were badly **damaged**.

left.label: damage a thing
left.text: You **damage** a thing: you harm or break it. The noun is **damage**.
examples: There was a lot of **damage** to the bike.

right.label: injure a person
right.text: You **injure** a person: you hurt them. The noun is **injury**.

lesson.text: Cars are **damaged**; people are **injured**. Never say ~~the driver was damaged~~.

exercises.prompt: Which word is being defined? People who are walking: ___ .
exercises.explanation: A pedestrian is a person walking.

exercises.prompt: Which word is being defined? The place where people usually walk, beside the road: the ___ .
exercises.explanation: The pavement is where pedestrians walk.

exercises.prompt: Which word is being defined? The place where two roads meet: a road ___ .
exercises.explanation: A road junction is where two roads meet.

exercises.prompt: Which word is being defined? The thing you put your foot on to stop a car: the ___ .
exercises.explanation: You press the brake to stop; the verb is also brake.

exercises.prompt: Match each road word with its meaning.

pairs.right: part of a road between two lines
it carries the road over a river
a big fast road between cities
the place where people cross the road

exercises.prompt: What does a sign saying '50 mph' tell you?
exercises.explanation: 50 mph is the speed limit - the fastest you may legally drive.

exercises.prompt: A sign says 'no overtaking'. What does it mean?
I didn't know where I was in the town centre. -> I got ___ in the town centre.
exercises.explanation: Get lost = not know where you are.

exercises.prompt: You can ask someone to tell you how to get here. -> You can ask someone to ___ you.
exercises.explanation: Direct someone = tell them how to get to a place.

exercises.prompt: I went through Ledbury to get to Malvern. -> I went to Malvern ___ Ledbury.
exercises.explanation: Go via a place = go through it to get to your destination.

exercises.prompt: We arrived unexpectedly by the river. -> We ___ up by the river.
exercises.explanation: End up = find yourself somewhere you didn't expect to be.

exercises.prompt: I turned left instead of right. -> I took the wrong ___ .
exercises.explanation: A turning is a corner where one road meets another.

exercises.prompt: He was driving too fast - over the ___ limit - and he lost control of the car.
exercises.explanation: The speed limit is the fastest you may legally drive.

exercises.prompt: He had to ___ to avoid a car on the other side of the road.
exercises.explanation: Swerve = change direction suddenly and without control.

exercises.prompt: In the end he ___ into a tree.
exercises.explanation: Crash into something = hit it hard with a vehicle.

exercises.prompt: Do we use damage or injure?
Put the words in order to describe the accident.
exercises.answer: The car was badly damaged, but the driver wasn't injured.
exercises.explanation: We damage things and injure people.

exercises.statement: A car was approaching means the car was coming closer.
